row.평가 축: 멀티모달 비망각(망각 효과·유지 성능·강건성, 지표 신뢰도 메타평가)
row.정의: MLLM 비망각 연구를 위한 오픈소스 프레임워크 겸 평가 프로토콜. 프라이버시·안전·저작권을 다루는 벤치마크 5종(본문 한 곳은 6종으로 표기), MLLM 8종(4개 모델군), 비망각 방법 12종을 공통 인터페이스로 통합한다. 평가는 Forget Quality, Model Utility, Robustness(모델·입력·출력 측면)로 나뉜다. 논문은 MLLMU-Bench 10% 망각 설정에서 10개 방법을 비교했고, MLLMU와 LLaVA-1.5-7B에서 13개 지표의 충실도(faithfulness)와 양자화·재학습 강건성을 메타평가했다.
row.대표 과제: 통합 파이프라인에서 방법별 망각 효과, 유지 성능, 강건성을 평가하고 지표의 충실도·강건성을 메타평가
row.대표 예시·설명: 이미지와 질문으로 구성된 멀티모달 QA 데이터에서 지정한 정보를 모델이 잊었는지, 나머지 능력이 유지되는지, 양자화·재학습·적대적 입력으로 정보가 복구되는지 확인하는 과제 설명
row.라이선스: MIT(저장소 코드·평가 스크립트 한정, 통합된 벤치마크 구성 요소는 각자 약관)
row.이용 시 유의사항: MIT 저작권 고지와 라이선스 전문을 사본에 포함해야 한다. 공식 저장소 README와 LICENSE 파일의 MIT는 저장소 저작물에 대한 표기이며, 저작권자로 CMU Locus Lab(OpenUnlearning 기반)과 Open-MMUnlearning 기여자가 적혀 있다. 이 프레임워크는 MLLMU-Bench, FIUBench, CLEAR, SafeEraser, CoVUBench 등 기존 벤치마크와 외부 모델·방법을 통합한 것이므로(논문 5쪽 표 1), 저장소의 MIT 표기가 이들 구성 요소 각각의 고유 약관을 대신하지 않는다. 각 구성 요소의 약관은 이용 전에 따로 확인해야 한다. 메타평가용 MLLMU 변형 데이터(질문 패러프레이즈, 답변 확장, 사실 변형 답변)는 GPT-4o 계열로 생성했으며 사실 정확성은 보증되지 않는다(논문 AI 사용 명시, 부록 A.3.4). 본문의 벤치마크 수 표기가 5종과 6종으로 일치하지 않는다. 방법 비교는 MLLMU 10% 망각 설정, 메타평가는 LLaVA-1.5-7B에 한정되며 논문 조건의 결과로서 현재 전역 리더보드가 아니다. 순위는 점수 정규화·집계 규칙에 의존한다.
row.lm-eval 지원: 논문 표 1에 LM-Eval 항목 수록(공식 카드에는 언급 없음)

english_copy.axis: Multimodal unlearning (forgetting effectiveness, retained utility, robustness; metric reliability meta-evaluation)
english_copy.definition: An open-source framework and evaluation protocol for MLLM unlearning. Through shared interfaces it integrates five benchmarks spanning privacy, safety, and copyright (one passage says six), eight MLLMs from four model families, and twelve unlearning methods. Evaluation covers Forget Quality, Model Utility, and Robustness (model-, input-, and output-side). The paper compares ten methods on MLLMU-Bench under the 10% forget setting and meta-evaluates 13 metrics for faithfulness and robustness to quantization and relearning on MLLMU with LLaVA-1.5-7B.
english_copy.task: Evaluate forgetting effectiveness, retained utility, and robustness of unlearning methods in one pipeline, and meta-evaluate metric faithfulness and robustness.
english_copy.example: Task description: on multimodal QA data pairing images with questions, check whether a model has forgotten designated information, whether unrelated capabilities are retained, and whether the information can be recovered through quantization, relearning, or adversarial inputs.

recommendations.metric: Overall aggregate score (Agg.), 0-1 unitless; equal-weight mean of Forget Quality, Model Utility and Robustness
recommendations.setting: Results reported in this paper (Table 2, page 7), not a current global leaderboard. Ten unlearning methods compared on MLLMU-Bench under the 10% forget setting with a common model preparation, hyperparameter search and evaluation protocol. For each method the checkpoint maximizing the mean of Forget Quality and Model Utility was selected, and robustness did not influence tuning. Finetune and Retain-Only reference rows are omitted.

screening.paper_title: Open-MMUnlearning: Unifying Methods and Evaluation for MLLM Unlearning
screening.abstract: As multimodal large language models (MLLMs) become more capable and widely deployed, concerns about privacy and safety have become increasingly pressing. Machine unlearning offers one approach to addressing these concerns by removing designated information from trained models while preserving unrelated capabilities. However, fragmented implementations and evaluation protocols, incomplete robustness testing, and limited understanding of metric reliability make progress in MLLM unlearning difficult to assess systematically. We introduce Open-MMUnlearning, an open-source, extensible framework that integrates target-model preparation, multimodal data processing, unlearning, and evaluation through shared interfaces and structured configurations. The framework supports five benchmarks spanning privacy, safety, and copyright, eight MLLMs from four model families, and twelve unlearning methods. Its evaluation suite jointly assesses forgetting effectiveness, retained utility, and robustness to model interventions, adversarial inputs, and membership inference attacks. Using a common evaluation protocol, we compare ten representative unlearning methods. In this comparison, GD and MIP-Editor tie for the highest overall score: GD achieves the highest Forget Quality, while MIP-Editor preserves more Model Utility. We further introduce a metric meta-evaluation protocol that tests faithfulness using models with controlled exposure to target knowledge and robustness under quantization and relearning. Among the thirteen evaluated metrics, BLEU achieves the highest aggregate reliability score. KS-Test attains the highest faithfulness AUC but performs less well on robustness. Together, the framework and these findings support reproducible comparison of MLLM unlearning methods and systematic assessment of evaluation reliability.
